name: NZ 8 m Digital Elevation Model (2012), Geographx
description: National 8 m raster elevation model built by Geographx mainly from LINZ Topo50 20 m contour data.
story: Geographx's 8 m national digital elevation model was compiled primarily from LINZ Topo50 20 m contour data, with point heights, interpolation and supplementary processing around waterways and coastlines. Roger Smith's 2012 account identifies it as the terrain source for the company's separate 4 m land-cover raster basemaps.

LINZ made the model available for reuse under a Creative Commons licence; the 2015 New Zealand Cartographic Society report distinguishes this open elevation model from Geographx's commercial natural-colour basemap. An 8 m grid interval is the raster spacing, not a claim of 8 m vertical or positional accuracy. The contour-derived surface was designed principally for cartographic visualisation, not for detailed terrain analysis, including precise hydrological, geotechnical or site-level modelling.

Later cartographic services reused this elevation resource. LINZ's published basemap reconstruction workflow calls for the 2012 8 m DEM and associated hillshade as inputs to TileMill alongside Topo50 and LCDB3.3. GNS and regional council services have also cited the Geographx model as a hillshade or terrain source. These downstream displays should not be mistaken for the separate original 4 m commercial imagery.
